title: Send the post-review summary within 24 hours
why_matters: The most powerful piece of paper around your probation review is the one you send within 24 hours of the meeting — yes / no / extended, what they liked, what they want different, what was agreed. Without it, two months from now nobody can quite remember what was decided. With it, the conversation has a written shape that survives.
steps: Within 24 hours of the review, draft a five-sentence summary: the decision, the concerns (if any), what you committed to, what your manager committed to, the next checkpoint.
Email it to your manager. Copy your evidence file.
If your manager amends — accept the amendment unless it materially changes what you remember being agreed. If it does, push back politely once in writing.
File the final version under Probation evidence — outcome. This is the document you'll return to at six months.
success_criteria: A five-sentence summary is sent within 24 hours. Manager has confirmed (or amended). The final version is filed in your evidence directory with the date.
reflection_prompt: Looking at the summary — what's the one thing in there that, if you do nothing about it, will quietly become a problem at the six-month mark?
